---
title: "Architecture"
description: >-
  How the plugin is put together: the scripts, the context menu, Fluent's blank-label trap, keyboard handling and how an attachment is chosen.
---

## The scripts

Four scripts are loaded in order into one plugin scope:

| | |
|---|---|
| `util.js` | parsing, sanitising, URL and shortcut helpers |
| `sheet.js` | the contact sheet's markup and sizing |
| `epub.js` | the EPUB-to-HTML pipeline |
| `zotlook.js` | windows, shortcuts, subprocesses, notes, contact sheets |

The page renderer runs apart from all of them, in `render.worker.js`. Strings
live in `locale/<locale>/zotlook.ftl`.

## The context menu

Entries are inserted into each window directly rather than through
`Zotero.MenuManager`.

That API accepts only an l10n id and never a plain label. An entry whose string
the main window's Fluent context cannot resolve therefore renders as an **empty
line** — no error, just a blank row in the menu. Inserting the entries here
keeps the label, and its English fallback, under the plugin's control.

## Fluent and the blank-label trap

Strings destined for a XUL `<button>` or `<menuitem>` must be written in
Fluent's attribute form:

```fluent
zotlook-menu-preview =
    .label = Quick Look
```

Those elements render their `label` **attribute** and ignore text content, which
a plain message value would set. That is the reason two rounds of menu entries
and a dropdown once came out blank. `<label>`, `<description>` and HTML
elements take the plain form.

## Keyboard handling

The plugin registers a listener on Zotero's items tree in the capture phase, so
it gets in front of Zotero's own Space handler.

Shortcuts are stored as strings such as `Alt+Space` or `Meta+y`. The final token
is read as a **physical key code** when it is longer than one character, and as
a **produced character** otherwise.

::: {.callout-note title="Why both forms"}
Space sits in the same place on every layout, so a code identifies it. The key
labelled Y on a QWERTZ keyboard, by contrast, reports the code `KeyZ` — so only
the produced character identifies the shortcut a user actually sees on their
keycaps.
:::

Changing a shortcut takes effect immediately.

## Choosing the defaults

A default that a system takes for itself can never fire, so the shipped
combinations avoid three separate hazards.

**macOS** binds Ctrl+Space and Ctrl+Option+Space to input sources, Cmd+Space to
Spotlight and Cmd+Option+Space to the Finder search window. The input-source
pair is dormant while only one keyboard layout is enabled and springs back the
moment a second one is added — so it counts as taken.

**A window manager** is the harder case, because it claims its combinations
before the application is asked at all. Alt+Space is the window menu on GNOME
and on Windows alike, which is why the contact sheet sits on **Ctrl+Shift+Space**
— free on all three systems, where plain Ctrl+Space is the input-method toggle
on two of them.

`ZotLookUtil.SHORTCUT_DEFAULTS` is the single list the plugin and the settings
pane both read. The pane's "Restore defaults" writes an explicit value rather
than clearing the preference, so its idea of the default has to be the same one;
a test holds that list against `prefs.js`, which repeats the values for Gecko's
preference parser.

## Choosing an attachment

Only one attachment is ever previewed, and only one contact sheet is ever built.

Candidates are **ordered first and then resolved one at a time**, stopping at
the first that works. Resolving them all would download every synced attachment
of every selected item only to discard all but one.

Attachments are classified by content type through Zotero's own predicates,
never by filename. The type setting is a ranking rather than a filter: every
type stays eligible, so one near the bottom is still used when nothing above it
is present.

## Annotations

Zotero keeps annotations in its database rather than in the file. When an
attachment has any, `Zotero.PDFWorker.export` writes a copy with them drawn in
and that copy is previewed.

Attachments without annotations are recognised before any work starts, and an
export is reused until an annotation is added or edited, so the common case
costs nothing.
